userStories.title: Telemetry event types and reporter config schema
acceptanceCriteria: When a subscriber registered via `bus.on("story:phase:completed", fn)` receives an emitted event, then its `phase` equals the emitted phase.
When a subscriber registered for `story:phase:completed` receives an emitted event, then its `costUsd` equals the emitted value.
When `postrun:phase:started` is emitted with phase `acceptance-setup`, then its subscriber receives `acceptance-setup` unchanged.
When `postrun:phase:completed` is emitted with a `details` payload, then its subscriber receives that payload unmodified.
When `story:phase:completed` is emitted, then `bus.onAll` receives it.
When an empty configuration is parsed, then `reporters.otel.detail` is `counts`.
When an empty configuration is parsed, then `reporters.otel.heartbeatIntervalMs` is `10000`.
When an empty configuration is parsed, then `reporters.otel.maxBatchSize` is `64`.
When an empty configuration is parsed, then `reporters.otel.flushIntervalMs` is `5000`.
When an empty configuration is parsed, then `reporters.otel.maxQueueSize` is `2048`.
When an empty configuration is parsed, then `reporters.otel.phases` is absent.

When `reporters.webhook.events` contains `onPhaseComplete`, then the parsed configuration retains that entry.

userStories.title: Story-phase event emission and outcome derivation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Emit one fail-open completion event for every `runPhase` invocation.

**Motivation** — There is no way to answer which phase consumed time and money.

**Approach** — `runPhase`'s existing `finally` block already computes the phase's exact cost via `scope.snapshot().totalCostUsd`. The phase event reuses `buildPhaseOutcomeLogData` rather than introducing a second derivation. `success === true` -> `passed`; `status === "skipped"` -> `skipped`; a thrown error -> `error`; otherwise `failed`. The function returns `null` for non-object output — emit `passed` with no `details`.

**Scope** — In: event emission, outcome/cost/duration semantics, subscriber fail-open behavior. Out: routing metadata and detail arms belong to US-003; reporter consumption belongs to US-005.

**Interface** — `story:step` is unchanged and serves as the start half. There is no `attempt` field: the *N*th `story:phase:completed` for a given `(storyId, phase)` pair is attempt *N*. Per-phase cost is the invocation's own scope total; never the accumulated `phaseCosts` entry.
acceptanceCriteria: When `runPhase` dispatches an operation returning `{ passed: true }`, then it emits exactly one `story:phase:completed` event.
When `runPhase` dispatches an operation, then the emitted event phase equals the operation name.
When an operation returns `{ passed: true }`, then the emitted outcome is `passed`.
When an operation returns `{ passed: false }`, then the emitted outcome is `failed`.
When an operation returns `{ status: "skipped" }`, then the emitted outcome is `skipped`.
When a dispatched operation throws, then the emitted outcome is `error`.
When a dispatched operation throws, then `runPhase` rethrows the original error unchanged.
When an operation returns a non-object value, then its emitted outcome is `passed`.
When an operation returns a non-object value, then its emitted event has no `details` field.
When an operation output makes `buildPhaseOutcomeLogData` report success, then the emitted outcome is `passed`.
When a `semantic-review` operation runs, then it emits an outcome even though deterministic outcome logging returns early.
When a phase completes, then its emitted `costUsd` equals that invocation scope snapshot total.
When a phase completes, then its emitted `durationMs` equals elapsed operation-dispatch time.
When a `story:phase:completed` subscriber throws, then `runPhase` returns the operation output normally.

routing.reasoning: One established dispatcher and its existing outcome helper need a localized event emission and exception-preservation tests.

userStories.title: Phase telemetry context and detail payloads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Propagate routed metadata to every phase and construct typed authoring, verdict, gate, review, and fix detail payloads.

**Motivation** — `sessionModel`, `testStrategy`, and `tier` are not reachable from `runPhase` as it stands.

**Approach** — Resolution — one readonly input-side slice on `CallContext`, populated where `ctx.routing` is in scope (`execution.ts:89-99`). Every `runPhase` call site inherits it through `ctx`, so correctness does not depend on remembering an argument. `sessionModel` comes from `isThreeSessionStrategy(ctx.routing.testStrategy)` — the existing SSOT. `rectification.ts:236` dispatches via `wrappedCallOp(cycleCtx: FixCycleContext, …)`; the slice must survive that hop.

**Scope** — In: post-clamp tier, routed strategy/session metadata, and all PhaseDetails arms. Out: base event/outcome emission is US-002; reporter mapping/export is US-005 onward.

**Interface** — verbatim:
```ts
type PhaseDetails =
  | { kind: "authoring"; role: "test-writer" | "implementer"; filesChanged: number; isolationPassed?: boolean }
  | { kind: "verdict"; role: "verifier" | "verify-scoped"; passed: boolean; failureCount: number }
  | { kind: "gate"; gate: "greenfield" | "full-suite" | "test-presence" | "lint" | "typecheck"; failureCount: number }
  | { kind: "review"; reviewer: "semantic" | "adversarial"; iteration: number; bySeverity: Record<FindingSeverity, number>; blockingCount: number; advisoryCount: number; items?: ReviewFindingSummary[] }
  | { kind: "fix"; strategy: string; findingsBefore: number };
```
`isolationPassed` is set only when `sessionModel === "three-session"`. Severity keys are `critical`, `error`, `warning`, `info`, `low`, and `unverifiable`; use `isBlockingSeverity(finding.severity, threshold)` for blocking/advisory counts. `items` is populated exclusively when `detail` is `verbose`.

The `fix` arm carries no `findingsAfter` — that is an iteration-level outcome known only after the cycle re-validates, i.e. after the fixing op's phase event has already been emitted. `strategy` and `findingsBefore` reach `runPhase` via a second readonly `CallContext` slice, `fixStrategy: { name: string; findingsBefore: number }`, populated per strategy in the loop at `src/findings/cycle.ts:286-291` (`FixCycleContext` is `CallContext & { storyId }` and carries no strategy information of its own).

`blockingCount` must be computed at the *configured* threshold. `buildPhaseDetails` today reads `adv?.blockingThreshold ?? "error"` from a cast of the op output, but `AdversarialReviewOutput` has no such field — the value is always `undefined` and always falls back to `"error"`. Persist the resolved threshold onto `AdversarialReviewOutput` from `verify()`'s `input.blockingThreshold`.

`items` is gated at emission, not at export: `story:phase:completed` fans out to every reporter including the webhook reporter, so dropping `items` only in the OTel exporter would still leak finding text. `buildPhaseDetails` takes `ctx.config` as a fourth argument (it is a pure 3-arg function today).
acceptanceCriteria: Running the execution stage for a story routed with `testStrategy` `"three-session-tdd"` emits phase events whose `sessionModel` is `"three-session"`.
Running the execution stage for a story routed with `testStrategy` `"three-session-tdd"` emits phase events whose `testStrategy` is `"three-session-tdd"`.
Running the execution stage for a story routed with `testStrategy` `"no-test"` emits phase events whose `sessionModel` is `"single-session"`.
Emitted phase events carry a `tier` equal to the model tier the execution stage resolved after its supported-tier clamp.
A phase dispatched through `runFixCycle` during a story routed as `"three-session-tdd"` emits `sessionModel` equal to `"three-session"`.
An `adversarial-review` operation emits `details` whose `kind` is `"review"` and whose `iteration` equals the number of times that operation has already completed for the same story.
An `adversarial-review` operation emits `details.bySeverity` counts keyed by the members of `FindingSeverity`, matching its normalized findings.

An `adversarial-review` operation configured with a `blockingThreshold` of `"warning"` emits a `details.blockingCount` equal to the number of its findings for which `isBlockingSeverity` returns true at `"warning"`, not at the `"error"` default.
An `implementer` operation in a three-session context emits `details.isolationPassed` equal to the operation's isolation result.
An `implementer` operation in a single-session context emits `details` with no `isolationPassed` field.
An `implementer` operation emits `details.filesChanged` equal to the number of files its output reports as changed.
A `test-writer` operation emits `details` whose `kind` is `"authoring"` and whose `role` is `"test-writer"`.
A `full-suite-gate` operation emits `details` whose `kind` is `"gate"` and whose `failureCount` equals the number of failures its output reports.
A `verifier` operation emits `details` whose `kind` is `"verdict"` and whose `passed` equals the operation's verdict.

An operation dispatched while the `fixStrategy` context slice is populated emits `details` whose `kind` is `"fix"`, whose `strategy` equals the slice's `name`, and whose `findingsBefore` equals the slice's `findingsBefore`.
With `detail` set to `"verbose"`, an `adversarial-review` operation emits `details.items` carrying each finding's `message`.

routing.reasoning: Routing metadata crosses execution, rectification, and dispatcher contexts and must agree with existing finding severity semantics.

userStories.title: Run-level phase events and enrichment
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Emit acceptance setup and enrich every run-level phase completion with duration, cost, and specific details.

**Motivation** — The pre-run `acceptance-setup` stage emits no bus event; final acceptance, deferred regression, and deferred review carry only a boolean `passed`.

**Approach** — `acceptance-setup` is newly emitted from `src/pipeline/stages/acceptance-setup.ts`. `acceptance`, `regression`, and `review` already emit and are enriched.

**Scope** — In: start/completion lifecycle events, details, elapsed duration correlation, and TUI fourth-phase tolerance. Out: reporter fan-out is US-005.

**Interface** — Widen `PostRunPhaseStartedEvent["phase"]` and `PostRunPhaseCompletedEvent["phase"]` to include `"acceptance-setup"`, and add `durationMs` / `details` to completed events (`costUsd` is declared on the event by US-001 but populating it is out of scope — see Out of Scope). Details are: `acceptance-setup`: `totalCriteria`, `testableCount`, `redFailCount`, `regenerated`; `acceptance`: `retries`, `failedACCount`, `fixStoriesCreated`; `regression`: `mode: "deferred" | "per-story" | "disabled"`, `failedTests`; `review`: `findingCount`, `anyFailed`.
acceptanceCriteria: Running the acceptance-setup stage emits a `postrun:phase:started` event whose `phase` is `"acceptance-setup"` before any acceptance test file is generated.
Running the acceptance-setup stage with a RED gate that fails emits `postrun:phase:completed` for `"acceptance-setup"` with `passed` true.
The `"acceptance-setup"` completion event's `details` carries `totalCriteria`, `testableCount`, and `redFailCount` equal to the values the stage records.
When every acceptance test already passes and the stage returns a skip result, the `"acceptance-setup"` completion event is still emitted.
The `"acceptance"` completion event's `details.retries` equals the retry count returned by the acceptance loop.
The `"acceptance"` completion event's `details.failedACCount` equals the number of failed acceptance criteria returned by the acceptance loop.
The `"acceptance"` completion event's `details.fixStoriesCreated` equals the number of fix stories the acceptance loop created.
The `"regression"` completion event's `details.mode` equals the configured regression gate mode.
The `"regression"` completion event's `details.failedTests` equals the number of failing tests the regression gate reported.
The `"review"` completion event's `details.findingCount` equals the number of deferred reviewers that reported a failure.
Every `postrun:phase:completed` event carries a `durationMs` measured from its matching `postrun:phase:started` event.
The TUI pipeline-bus subscriber handles a `postrun:phase:started` event with `phase` `"acceptance-setup"` without throwing and records it as a running phase.

routing.reasoning: Several independent lifecycle owners and UI compatibility must be coordinated.

userStories.title: Reporter fan-out for phase hooks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Map story and run phase bus events into optional reporter hooks and webhook event filtering.

**Motivation** — Reporters are wired to the pipeline bus by existing convention, but have no per-phase visibility.

**Approach** — Add fan-out for four bus events. The file's repeated per-reporter fan-out block is extracted into a local helper as part of this wiring rather than copy-pasted four more times; this is an implementation detail of the same change, not separate refactoring.

**Scope** — In: `story:step`, story completion, post-run start, and post-run completion mapping; hook isolation; webhook event support. Out: OTel exporter queue/tree behavior belongs to US-006 through US-008.

**Interface** — `PhaseStartEvent` and `PhaseCompleteEvent` use `scope: "story" | "run"`; `storyId` is present iff `scope === "story"`. Both hooks optional; existing reporters are unaffected.
acceptanceCriteria: After `wireReporters`, emitting `story:step` invokes the registered reporter's `onPhaseStart` with `scope` `"story"` and a `storyId` equal to the event's `storyId`.
The `onPhaseStart` invocation triggered by `story:step` carries a `phase` equal to the event's `step`.
After `wireReporters`, emitting `story:phase:completed` invokes `onPhaseComplete` with `scope` `"story"`.
The `onPhaseComplete` invocation triggered by `story:phase:completed` carries an `outcome` equal to the event's `outcome`.
The `onPhaseComplete` invocation triggered by `story:phase:completed` carries a `costUsd` equal to the event's `costUsd`.
After `wireReporters`, emitting `postrun:phase:started` invokes `onPhaseStart` with `scope` equal to `"run"`.
The `onPhaseStart` invocation triggered by `postrun:phase:started` has no `storyId` field.
After `wireReporters`, emitting `postrun:phase:completed` invokes `onPhaseComplete` with `scope` `"run"`.
Every phase event delivered to a reporter hook carries the `runId` that `wireReporters` was constructed with.
A registered reporter that does not implement `onPhaseComplete` is skipped when `story:phase:completed` is emitted.
When the first of two registered reporters throws from `onPhaseComplete`, the second reporter's `onPhaseComplete` is still invoked.
Emitting `run:started` after the new wiring still invokes the reporter's `onRunStart`.
Invoking the unsubscribe function returned by `wireReporters` stops further `onPhaseComplete` invocations for subsequently emitted events.
A webhook reporter configured with `events` containing only `"onPhaseComplete"` posts an envelope whose `type` is `"onPhaseComplete"` when that hook fires.
A webhook reporter configured with `events` containing only `"onPhaseComplete"` performs no request when `onPhaseStart` fires.

routing.reasoning: This extends one existing subscriber and one existing webhook factory using already-established optional-hook isolation.

userStories.title: Batch queue and traceparent
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace end-of-run-only export with bounded incremental batches and W3C trace parent adoption.

**Motivation** — Nothing is visible while a run is in flight, so a run that hangs mid-phase emits nothing.

**Approach** — Bounded FIFO queue. Flush on `maxBatchSize` (64), on `flushIntervalMs` (5000) via a re-armed `setTimeout` + `clearTimeout` (`setInterval` is banned; the cancellable-handle exception applies and is documented at the call site), or on `flushNow()`. Overflow at `maxQueueSize` (2048) drops oldest and counts drops. One retry per failed batch, then drop. All I/O through the existing `PostJsonDeps` injection.

**Scope** — In: queue, time/size/explicit flush, retry/drop reporting, teardown, and traceparent parsing. Out: span parenting/aggregate metrics are US-007 and heartbeat/redaction/lifecycle is US-008; de-duplication is deferred.

**Interface** — Root span parent is `W3C TRACEPARENT` env when valid, else root. Traceparent malformed or all-zero is ignored.
acceptanceCriteria: A run whose stories all complete still exports a run span carrying the run's total cost, preserving the end-of-run export behaviour this story replaces.
Enqueuing `maxBatchSize` spans issues exactly one export request carrying every enqueued span.
Enqueuing fewer than `maxBatchSize` spans issues an export request once `flushIntervalMs` has elapsed.
Calling `flushNow` exports pending spans before `flushIntervalMs` has elapsed.
Enqueuing beyond `maxQueueSize` discards the oldest entries.
After an overflow, the queue reports a drop count equal to the number of entries discarded.
An overflow logs one warning per threshold crossing rather than one per discarded entry.
A failed export request is retried exactly once.
`flushNow` completes without throwing once the retry budget for a failing export is exhausted.
A span enqueued while an export request is in flight is included in a subsequent export.
After the queue is torn down, no export request is issued even once `flushIntervalMs` has elapsed.
A valid W3C traceparent value produces a run span whose parent span id equals that value's span id.
A malformed traceparent value produces a run span with no parent span id.
A traceparent whose trace id is all zeros produces a run span with no parent span id.

routing.reasoning: Concurrent bounded delivery, timer ownership, retry, and trace-context parsing are high-risk.

userStories.title: Span tree and phase metrics
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Export completed work as run/story/phase spans and bounded-cardinality aggregate metrics.

**Motivation** — There is no way to answer how often adversarial review rejects or how many rectification iterations a story needs.

**Approach** — OTLP payloads stay hand-built — no `@opentelemetry/*` dependency. `nax.run` is root, `nax.story` is one per story, and `nax.phase` is one per completion. Run-scope phases parent directly to run. `buildHistogramPoint` emits `explicitBounds` + `bucketCounts` + `count` + `sum`.

**Scope** — In: span-tree module, phase spans, histograms/counters/resource attributes. Out: heartbeat/detail redaction and final flush are US-008.

**Interface** — Fixed duration boundaries `[100, 500, 1000, 5000, 15000, 60000, 300000, 900000]`; cost `[0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5]`. Aggregate metric dimensions are phase, outcome, tier, test_strategy, session_model; `run_id` and `story_id` are excluded. Export `nax.phase.duration`, `nax.phase.cost_usd`, `nax.review.findings`, `nax.fix.iterations`, and `nax.escalations`.
acceptanceCriteria: A `story:phase:completed` event produces a span whose parent span id equals its story span's id.
A story's span carries a parent span id equal to the run span's id.
A run-scope phase completion produces a span whose parent span id equals the run span's id.
Emitting a `story:phase:completed` event produces an exported `nax.phase.duration` data point whose recorded value equals the event's `durationMs`.
Emitting a `story:phase:completed` event produces an exported `nax.phase.cost_usd` data point whose recorded value equals the event's `costUsd`.
A histogram data point's bucket-count list has exactly one more entry than its explicit-bounds list.
A histogram data point's `sum` equals the total of the values recorded into it.
A phase-duration metric data point carries no attribute named `run_id` and none named `story_id`.
A phase-duration metric data point's attribute names are exactly `phase`, `outcome`, `tier`, `test_strategy`, and `session_model`.
A phase-duration histogram data point's explicit bounds are `[100, 500, 1000, 5000, 15000, 60000, 300000, 900000]`, and a phase-cost histogram data point's are `[0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5]`.
A phase span carries a `nax.test_strategy` attribute equal to the event's `testStrategy`.
An `adversarial-review` phase event produces an exported `nax.review.findings` counter data point carrying a `severity` attribute.
A rectification phase event produces an exported `nax.fix.iterations` counter data point carrying a `strategy` attribute.
A `story:escalated` event produces an exported `nax.escalations` counter data point carrying a `to_tier` attribute.
Every exported payload carries a `service.name` resource attribute equal to the configured service name.
Every exported payload carries a `nax.run_id` resource attribute equal to the current run's id.

routing.reasoning: Existing hand-built OTLP helpers are extended across the reporter and queue with a new parentage helper and bounded metrics surface.

userStories.title: Heartbeat, redaction, and flush lifecycle
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make active runs observable, enforce detail redaction, and flush safely on normal and abnormal exit.

**Motivation** — A run that hangs mid-phase emits nothing at all.

**Approach** — Every `heartbeatIntervalMs` (default 10000; `0` disables) emit gauges `nax.run.active` (=1), `nax.run.phase_elapsed_ms`, and `nax.run.cost_usd`, with attributes `{run_id, feature, project, story_id, phase, tier, test_strategy}`. The flush and heartbeat stop are driven from the reporter's own `onRunEnd`, with `NaxPlugin.teardown()` as an idempotent backstop.

**Scope** — In: heartbeat cadence, counts/verbose redaction boundary, onRunEnd and teardown delivery. Out: `US-008 only: persisting heartbeat state across a process restart is deferred; a restarted run emits a new series.` Agent prompts, agent output, diffs, and source-code excerpts remain excluded at every detail level.

**Interface** — `items` is the only per-finding payload and is gated. It is populated exclusively when `detail` is `verbose`, and carries `Finding.message`. Under default `counts` it is absent entirely. Agent prompts, agent output, diffs, and source excerpts are never exported. `onRunEnd` with no preceding onRunStart exports a best-effort root span whose start is back-computed from duration.
acceptanceCriteria: With `heartbeatIntervalMs` set to a positive value, an export request containing a `nax.run.active` gauge of value 1 is issued once that interval has elapsed.
A heartbeat export request contains a `nax.run.phase_elapsed_ms` gauge whose value is the elapsed time since the most recent phase event.
A heartbeat export request contains a `nax.run.cost_usd` gauge whose value equals the run's accumulated cost.
A heartbeat gauge carries a `phase` attribute equal to the most recently completed phase's name.
A heartbeat gauge carries `run_id`, `feature`, `project`, `story_id`, `tier`, and `test_strategy` attributes alongside `phase`.
With `heartbeatIntervalMs` set to 0, no heartbeat export request is issued regardless of elapsed time.
After `onRunEnd`, no further heartbeat export request is issued.
With `detail` set to `"counts"`, an emitted review phase's `details` carries no `items` array.
With `detail` set to `"counts"`, no exported payload contains any review finding's `message` text.
With `detail` set to `"verbose"`, an exported payload contains a span event carrying a review finding's `message`.
With `detail` set to `"verbose"`, every exported file path is relative to the repository root.
No log record produced during export contains a resolved header value.
Invoking `onRunEnd` without any preceding `run:completed` bus event exports every queued span.
Invoking `onRunEnd` without any preceding `run:completed` bus event stops the heartbeat.
Invoking the plugin's `teardown` after `onRunEnd` has already completed issues no additional export request.
Invoking `onRunEnd` with no preceding `onRunStart` exports a run span whose start time is back-computed from the reported run duration.

routing.reasoning: Timer cleanup, abnormal-exit delivery, and sensitive-detail filtering cross the reporter lifecycle and cleanup seam.

analysis: This is a cross-cutting enhancement to an existing Bun/TypeScript pipeline, not a greenfield change. `src/pipeline/event-bus.ts:149-187` already emits `story:step` starts and three typed post-run phases, but has no story completion event and no duration/cost/details on post-run completions. `src/plugins/extensions.ts:371-386` defines IReporter with only run-start, story-complete, and run-end hooks; `src/pipeline/subscribers/reporters.ts:28-176` maps those bus events with per-reporter try/catch, so new hooks must retain optional-hook compatibility and per-reporter failure isolation. `src/execution/story-orchestrator/run-phase.ts:142-258` is the canonical per-op dispatcher: it emits `story:step`, opens a CostAggregator scope, and in finally accumulates the invocation cost; it is the correct fail-open emission seam, but must emit the single scope snapshot rather than accumulated `phaseCosts`. `src/execution/story-orchestrator-logging.ts:18-50` contains the outcome SSOT and must be reused. `src/pipeline/stages/execution.ts:67-99` owns the post-clamp model tier and routed test strategy needed to populate the readonly CallContext slice; rectification calls `runPhase` through FixCycleContext (`src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts:236-297`), so the slice must survive structural context reuse. `src/pipeline/stages/acceptance-setup.ts`, `src/execution/runner-completion.ts:133-213`, and `src/execution/lifecycle/run-completion.ts:137-287` own run-level phase emission; the TUI subscriber at `src/tui/hooks/usePipelineBusEvents.ts:227-246` narrows its accepted phase union. Reporter configuration is centralized in `src/config/schemas-reporters.ts:6-63`, and webhook filtering in `src/plugins/builtin/webhook-reporter/index.ts:14-44` follows ReporterEventSchema. The current OTel reporter (`src/plugins/builtin/otel-reporter/index.ts:26-109`) buffers story-complete events and posts only during onRunEnd; `otlp.ts:1-119` has hand-built trace/metric payload helpers and reporter-shared postJson dependency injection. The redesign must preserve hand-built OTLP and injectable I/O while introducing bounded, serialized incremental delivery and W3C traceparent parsing. `src/execution/lifecycle/run-cleanup.ts:116-140` directly invokes reporter.onRunEnd on abnormal exits, whereas normal completion is bus-delivered; flushing and heartbeat shutdown must be owned by onRunEnd and teardown must be idempotent. Existing focused tests are at `test/unit/pipeline/subscribers/reporters.test.ts`, `test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator-logging.test.ts`, acceptance-setup test files under `test/unit/pipeline/stages/`, and `test/unit/plugins/builtin/otel-reporter.test.ts`. Main compatibility risks are public plugin contracts/config defaults, cardinality-sensitive OTLP dimensions, timer cleanup, abort-path delivery, and finding-data redaction. Migration is additive through optional hooks and defaults; existing reporters remain valid, webhook configuration accepts new event names, and the old end-of-run export is replaced only after the queue preserves the root-span behavior.
outOfScope: OTLP logs export (`/v1/logs`) is deferred; the existing structured JSONL logger is unchanged.
A nax-side aggregator daemon (a `nax monitor` process) is not built; each run exports directly to its configured collector.
Trace sampling, gRPC OTLP transport, and alerting rules are delegated to the OTel collector and backend, not implemented in nax.
Histogram bucket boundaries are fixed constants and are deliberately not configurable.
Adopting `@opentelemetry/*` SDK packages is rejected; OTLP payloads stay hand-built and dependency-free.
Changes to cost accounting are excluded; costs are read from the existing `CostAggregator` scopes.
Exporting agent prompts, agent output, diffs, or source-code excerpts is excluded at every detail level.

US-003 only: renaming `reporters.otel.detail` to a reporter-neutral key is deferred. It gates the bus payload for every reporter, so its name understates its reach; a rename needs a config migration shim and is not worth coupling to this feature.

US-004 only: populating `costUsd` on `postrun:phase:completed` is deferred. The field is declared on the event by US-001 but no post-run phase has a cost scope to read from; producers leave it absent.

US-004 only: a real `quarantined` count on the regression completion is deferred. `QuarantineMemo` (`src/verification/flake-triage.ts`) exposes only `has()` and `add()` — no count accessor — and adding one is out of scope for this feature; the field is omitted rather than reported as a false `0`.
US-006 only: de-duplicating spans when two processes export under the same run id is deferred.
US-008 only: persisting heartbeat state across a process restart is deferred; a restarted run emits a new series.
